messages:
Marta: Quick sync: observed sustained latency regressions on dedicated shard 'theta-reserved-2' in us-east-1 at 09:40 UTC. Not thermal.
Ryan: Which hosts?
Marta: theta-2-11 and theta-2-12. Both show kernel txq pileups and high softirq rates.
Anika: Any tenant prefetching or background copy jobs?
Marta: From S3 logs, tenant 'dataforge' started bulk retrievals around 09:38, ~8 GB in a minute.
Ops-Bot: Alert: egress-congestion theta-reserved-2 (09:40 UTC). Auto-evac for 1 latency pod.
Samir: This pattern keeps repeating. We need a durable policy: per-pool egress reservation or allocator-level awareness.
Ryan: Short-term mitigation options: tc tbf on affected hosts, or move the bulk job to shared-burst pool. Which is quicker?
Anika: tc tbf is the fastest; I can apply `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 4gbit burst 32k latency 50ms` on both hosts.
Ling: Product will want to know how often Dedicated customers get noisy neighbors. If we propose egress carveouts it affects pricing.
DevInfra-Bot: Enqueue job apply-tc-theta-2-11 by Anika. JobID: job-5567.
Marta: Applied tc on theta-2-11/12. Tail latency improved ~45% in 2m and eviction stopped.
Anika: eBPF shows the heavy flow on PID 4321 (s3fetch). We labeled tenant 'dataforge' traffic as bulk-transfer.
Ryan: Good. Follow-ups: 1) allocator NIC-aware scoring, 2) prefetch/manager-level throttles, 3) RFC for egress carveout for Dedicated.
Samir: I'll compute cost of reserved egress per pool across us-east AZs.
Ling: I'll write a short blurb for product about SLA tradeoffs.
Marta: Incident note queued. End.
